key_insight: A physics-based CCD noise synthesis pipeline can generate realistic, interpretable noisy–clean image pairs for astronomical imaging, enabling effective supervised denoising without relying on scarce real paired data.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of physically realistic paired training data and the need for interpretable, reproducible noise models in astronomical CCD denoising workflows.
method: Construct a modular, physics-based simulator of CCD noise formation that models key stages (photon shot noise, dark current, pixel defects, readout electronics and digitization).
Use the simulator to synthesize realistic noisy–clean image pairs for training and augmenting learning-based denoisers.
Validate synthetic noise by matching statistical signatures to real observations and integrate the pipeline with standard calibration/denoising workflows.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with reproducible, physically grounded training data and diagnostics that improve denoiser generalization and scientific interpretability, reducing reliance on hard-to-obtain real paired datasets.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: photon → sensor → electronics → digitized image (annotate noise sources at each stage).
Side-by-side image triplet: clean ground truth, synthetic noisy image, denoised result.
Stacked bar or pie chart of noise contributions (shot noise, dark current, read noise, quantization) to show relative importance.
Statistical comparison plots (histograms, power spectra) demonstrating synthetic vs. real noise agreement.
paper_title: Denoising the Deep Sky: Physics-Based CCD Noise Formation for Astronomical Imaging
paper_authors: Shuhong Liu, Xining Ge, Ziying Gu, Lin Gu, Ziteng Cui
